# FAQ {.unnumbered}

## Process

```{=html}
<div class="accordion" id="accordionProcess">
  <div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="processHeading1">
      <button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#processCollapse1" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="processCollapse1">
        How much time should I spend on my thesis?
      </button>
    </h2>
    <div id="processCollapse1" class="accordion-collapse collapse" aria-labelledby="processHeading1" data-bs-parent="#accordionProcess">
      <div class="accordion-body">
        Bachelor's thesis in this program is worth 12 ECTS. This is equivalent to 336 hours of work. This averages to about 16 hours per week for the entire thesis period. It is very likely that you will need less time. At the same time, it is also likely that you will have weeks where you are spending less time on the thesis (e.g., during exam weeks, while waiting for feedback, etc.). Therefore, it is important to be mindful of the time you have available per week in order to successfully complete this project.
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="processHeading2">
      <button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#processCollapse2" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="processCollapse2">
        I heard from my friends that they are doing something differently. Why are we not expected to do it the same way?
      </button>
    </h2>
    <div id="processCollapse2" class="accordion-collapse collapse" aria-labelledby="processHeading2" data-bs-parent="#accordionProcess">
      <div class="accordion-body">
        A thesis project, and generally any scientific project, does not have one way of being done. There are many valid, acceptable, and evidence-supported approaches that can be taken depending on both needs of the project and the supervisor's preferred way of working. If you believe something can be done better, I am very happy to learn about your idea and potentially integrate it! A thesis project is a two-way street, so in the end both you and I will learn something new from it.
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
    <div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="processHeading3">
      <button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#processCollapse3" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="processCollapse3">
        What if I am running out of time, and can see that I will not be able to submit a section by the agreed deadline?
      </button>
    </h2>
    <div id="processCollapse3" class="accordion-collapse collapse" aria-labelledby="processHeading3" data-bs-parent="#accordionProcess">
      <div class="accordion-body">
        If this is just about a thesis section (e.g., introduction, methods, ...) and NOT the final, official product, please let me know ASAP about your delay. It is perfectly normal to have off-days or weeks, and realizing you need a bit more time because of it. I am very happy to work with you to make this work, however, I can only do so if you let me know about your delay on time. 
        For example, if you are three days away from the deadline, and know that there is no way you will be done on time, you should let me know. Generally, it is fine to be a day or two late, and I will not penalize you for this (i.e., it will not affect your process grade) if you communicated it promptly. However, being late does mean you might get feedback later, since I plan time for going over submissions and it is often very soon after the deadline.
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Content

```{=html}
<div class="accordion" id="accordionContent">
  <div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="contentHeading1">
      <button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#contentCollapse1" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="contentCollapse1">
        How many references should I include in my thesis?
      </button>
    </h2>
    <div id="contentCollapse1" class="accordion-collapse collapse" aria-labelledby="contentHeading1" data-bs-parent="#accordionContent">
      <div class="accordion-body">
        This is a very common question, and it is one that (unfortunately for you) does not have an answer. In my bachelor's thesis I included 71, but I have read theses that included anywhere from 25 to 100+. The number of references does <b>not</b> provide any indication for the quality of the written work. However, lack of references can lead to plagiarism, unsupported claims, weak arguments, and worse final evaluation. Therefore, always remember to provide references for <b>all</b> of the claims/arguments you make, even if it is something you consider general knowledge.
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Special circumstances

```{=html}
<div class="accordion" id="accordionSpecial">
  <div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="specialHeading1">

        What if I have to hand in my final thesis later?
      </button>
    </h2>
    <div id="specialCollapse1" class="accordion-collapse collapse" aria-labelledby="specialHeading1" data-bs-parent="#accordionSpecial">

However, you are free to contact me for advice on this matter.

  </div>
</div>
```
